title: The night at Muzdalifah
hookLine: a night under the sky and pebbles gathered

lines: THE PRAYER IS AHEAD OF YOU.
cards: The sun is down over Arafah, and nobody has prayed maghrib, the sunset prayer. A whole crowd is moving off the plain with it still waiting.
On the road, Usama ibn Zayd, riding behind the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, reminds him: the prayer, Messenger of God. The answer comes back: the prayer is ahead of you.
Ahead, in the dark, is a stretch of open ground between Arafah and Mina. Tonight the pilgrims sleep there, under the sky. Today, the night at Muzdalifah.

teach.b: The step-by-step telling of this night comes from Jabir ibn Abdullah, whose account of the Prophet's Hajj is kept in Sahih Muslim. First, the prayers.
When they reach Muzdalifah, he prays maghrib and isha together, with one call to prayer, and nothing prayed between them. Second, the sleep.
Then, Jabir says, he lay down until dawn. That's the whole report of the night. After a day of standing in du'a, the account describes rest.
Some scholars point out what isn't there: no long night vigil is described, and they take the sleep itself as part of what the Prophet did. Third, the mercy. Not everyone stays until dawn.

Ibn Abbas reports that he was among the weaker members of the Prophet's household who were sent on ahead during the night. Jurists draw on that permission for the elderly, the unwell, and those caring for them.
At dawn he prays fajr, then goes to the place the Qur'an calls the sacred monument, al-Mash'ar al-Haram, where Surah Al-Baqarah tells the pilgrims to remember God as He has guided them.

teach.h: THE PRAYER IS AHEAD OF YOU.
teach.b: He faces the qiblah, praises God, and stays until the sky is bright, then moves on before the sun comes up.
And the pebbles: pilgrims often pick up small stones here for the next morning's rite, though some schools allow gathering them elsewhere too.
A night on the ground, a pocket of pebbles, and nothing between the sleeper and the sky.

how: After sunset on the day of Arafah, pilgrims travel to Muzdalifah, pray maghrib and isha together, spend the night on open ground, and gather pebbles for the stoning; the elderly and weak may move on during the night.

games.q: what does “the night at muzdalifah” mean?
o: after Arafah: two prayers joined, then sleep in the open
a night kept awake in prayer beside the Ka'ba
the evening pilgrims stone the three pillars at Mina

games.q: the night at muzdalifah — tap the pairs.
p: told the night step by step

s: pilgrims pray maghrib at Arafah before they leave
they leave after sunset and pray maghrib and isha together at Muzdalifah.
in Jabir's account, the Prophet lay down until dawn
after the two prayers, he slept until fajr.
no one may leave Muzdalifah before dawn
Ibn Abbas was sent ahead in the night with the weaker members of the household.

games.q: you're riding off the plain of Arafah. the sun has set and maghrib hasn't been prayed. what do you do?
o: stop on the road and pray maghrib now.
keep going, and pray maghrib and isha together at Muzdalifah.
turn back and pray at Arafah.
games.why: when Usama reminds him of the prayer, the Prophet says the prayer is ahead of you, and joins the two prayers at Muzdalifah.

practice: Lie down on the floor, or sit low, close to the ground, and feel what's holding you up; for now nothing is asked of you except to be still, the way the pilgrims lie on that open ground.
If you pray, say a quiet alhamdulillah for the day that's ending; if not, name one thing today asked of you, and set it down.

wordCard.voice: The night at Muzdalifah. The night after Arafah: two prayers joined, sleep on open ground, remembrance at dawn, and pebbles gathered for the morning. Today's word.

orig.note: the open ground between Arafah and Mina where pilgrims spend the night.

carryVoice: Your line: a night under the sky. After the long standing, rest is part of the journey too. Sleep well.
